lessons.title: What is a Program
lessons.goal: A program is just a list of instructions, and by the end of this lesson you will know how Python reads them.

lessons.title: print() Basics
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how print() puts text on the screen.

lessons.title: Comments
lessons.goal: This lesson covers comments, which are notes you leave in your code so people can understand it.

lessons.title: Many Lines of Output
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how several print() calls make several lines of output.

lessons.title: Strings and Quotes
lessons.goal: This lesson covers strings, which is what Python calls text, and how to pick the right quotes so your text does not break.

lessons.title: Fancy print()
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to print several values on one line and how to make a blank line.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.goal: This lesson covers variables, which let you store a value once and reuse it wherever you need it.

lessons.title: Changing Variables
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to update a variable so it holds a new value.

lessons.title: Using Answers
lessons.goal: This lesson covers input(), which lets you ask a question, store the answer, and use it in your program.

lessons.title: Data Types & Casting
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know the three main beginner data types and how to convert between them so you can do math.

lessons.title: Plus and Minus
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how Python adds and subtracts numbers with + and -.

lessons.title: Multiply and Divide
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how Python multiplies with * and divides with /.

lessons.title: Order of Operations
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know that Python multiplies and divides before it adds and subtracts, and how parentheses change that.

lessons.title: Float Division
lessons.goal: This lesson covers float division, and why / always gives back a decimal.

lessons.title: Integer Division
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how // divides and keeps only the whole number part.

lessons.title: Remainder
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how % finds the leftover after dividing into whole groups.

lessons.title: Text into Numbers
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to turn text that looks like a number into a real int or float so you can do math with it.

lessons.title: Multi-step Math
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to break a bigger calculation into clear steps using variables.

lessons.title: The math Module
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to import the math module and use a few of its tools.

lessons.title: Useful math Tools
lessons.goal: This lesson covers a few handy tools: abs, round, min, max, and math.ceil / math.floor.

lessons.title: True and False
lessons.goal: This lesson covers booleans, which are the values True and False.

lessons.title: Comparing Values
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know the comparison operators that give back True or False.

lessons.title: if
lessons.goal: This lesson covers the if statement, which runs code only when a condition is True.

lessons.title: else
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how else runs when the if condition is False.

lessons.title: elif
lessons.goal: This lesson covers elif, which is another check that only runs if the earlier checks were False.

lessons.title: Many Branches
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will practice longer if, elif, and else chains that pick one outcome out of many choices.

lessons.title: and
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how and needs both sides to be True.

lessons.title: or
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how or is True when at least one side is True.

lessons.title: not
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how not flips True to False and False to True.

lessons.title: Complex Conditions
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will combine and, or, and not, and use parentheses to keep the meaning clear.

lessons.title: Why Loops
lessons.goal: This lesson covers why programs need repetition, and why copying the same line many times is a clue that a loop would help.

lessons.title: for Loops
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how a for loop visits each item in a list and runs an indented block once per item.

lessons.title: range() Basics
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how range() makes a sequence of numbers so a for loop can repeat a fixed number of times.

lessons.title: range() Start and Step
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know the start and step parts of range(), so you can count from any number and skip by a fixed jump.

lessons.title: Looping and Totals
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to keep a running total inside a loop by adding to a variable each time through.

lessons.title: while Loops
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how a while loop repeats as long as a condition is True, using a counter that changes each time.

lessons.title: while Counters
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will practice while loops that count up or down with a clear counter pattern.

lessons.title: Loops That Stop Safely
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to keep while loops finite by always updating the counter so the condition can become False.

lessons.title: if Inside Loops
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to put an if statement inside a loop so each value can be checked and handled differently.

lessons.title: Filter with Loops
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to filter values with a loop, so you print or count only the items that match a rule.

lessons.title: Why Functions
lessons.goal: This lesson covers why programs use functions, which let you name a chunk of work once and reuse it instead of copying the same lines.

lessons.title: Defining and Calling
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to define a function with def and run it by calling its name with parentheses.

lessons.title: One Parameter
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to give a function one parameter, so the same function can work with different values each time you call it.

lessons.title: Multiple Parameters
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to define and call functions with more than one parameter so you can pass several values at once.

lessons.title: Return Values
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to send a result back out of a function with return, so the caller can use that value.

lessons.title: Using What You Return
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to store a return value in a variable and use it later in prints or other calculations.

lessons.title: Functions Calling Functions
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how one function can call another, so you can build bigger behavior out of small pieces.

lessons.title: Designing with Functions
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to break a bigger program into small, well named functions that each do one job.

lessons.title: What is a List
lessons.goal: This lesson covers what a list is, and why one list can hold many values in order.

lessons.title: Creating Lists
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to create lists with square brackets, including empty lists and lists that mix types.

lessons.title: Indexes
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to pick one item from a list using its index number, which starts from 0.

lessons.title: Changing Items
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to replace a value that is already in a list by assigning to an index.

lessons.title: append and insert
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to grow a list by adding items at the end with append, or at a chosen spot with insert.

lessons.title: remove and pop
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to take items out of a list with remove (by value) and pop (by index).

lessons.title: for over Lists
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to visit every item in a list with a for loop.

lessons.title: Totals from Lists
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to add up the numbers in a list with a running total inside a for loop.

lessons.title: List Methods
lessons.goal: This lesson covers a few handy list tools: sort, in, count, and index.

lessons.title: Building Lists
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will put your list skills together by starting with an empty list, appending in a loop, and then using the finished list.

lessons.title: Lists Inside Lists
lessons.goal: This lesson covers what a 2D list is, which is a list where each item is another list, and how to picture it as a small grid.

lessons.title: Reading Rows
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to read one whole row from a 2D list using a single index.

lessons.title: Cells and Columns
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to read one cell with two indexes, and how to read a column down the grid.

lessons.title: Changing a Cell
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to update one cell in a 2D list by assigning to grid[row][col].

lessons.title: Nested Loops
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to visit every cell in a 2D list with a loop inside another loop.

lessons.title: Printing a Grid
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to print a 2D list so it looks like a neat grid on the screen.

lessons.title: Searching a Grid
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to search a 2D list for a value and report whether it was found.

lessons.title: Grid Mini Project
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will combine your 2D list skills by building a small grid, changing cells, printing it, and then totalling or searching the values.

lessons.title: What is a Dictionary
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how a dictionary stores labeled facts as key and value pairs.

lessons.title: Creating Dictionaries
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to create a dictionary with curly braces and key: value pairs.

lessons.title: Looking Up Keys
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to look up a value with square brackets and a key.

lessons.title: Adding Keys
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to add a brand new key to a dictionary.

lessons.title: Updating Values
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to update a value that is already stored under a key.

lessons.title: Removing Keys
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to remove a key with pop and see the dictionary shrink.

lessons.title: Looping Keys
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how a for loop visits each key in a dictionary.

lessons.title: Looping Items
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how .items() gives you each key and value together in a loop.

lessons.title: Safe Lookup with get
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how .get() looks up a key safely, without crashing when it is missing.

lessons.title: Dictionary Methods
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will practice a few handy dictionary tools: in, get, keys, values, and pop together.

lessons.title: What is a File
lessons.goal: This lesson covers what a practice file is, and that these files live in a fake folder on this page and not on your real computer.

lessons.title: Opening and Reading
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to open a practice file and read all of its text with read().

lessons.title: Reading Lines
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to read a file one line at a time with a for loop.

lessons.title: Writing Files
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how to create or overwrite a practice file with mode "w" and write().

lessons.title: Append Mode
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how append mode adds new text to the end of a file without erasing what is already there.

lessons.title: with open
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how with open opens a file and closes it for you when the block ends.

lessons.title: Processing File Text
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to split a line from a file into pieces and work with each part.

lessons.title: File Mini Project
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will put reading, writing, and processing together in one small file project.

lessons.title: What is an Error
lessons.goal: This lesson covers what an error is, and why it is a clue and not a sign that you failed.

lessons.title: Reading Error Messages
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to read the parts of an error message to find what went wrong.

lessons.title: Common Errors
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to recognize three common errors: NameError, ZeroDivisionError, and TypeError.

lessons.title: try
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how a try block marks code that might fail.

lessons.title: except
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how except catches an error from try so the program can keep going.

lessons.title: Friendly Messages
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to show a friendly message in except instead of a scary crash.

lessons.title: Specific except
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how to catch specific error types like ZeroDivisionError and ValueError.

lessons.title: Error Practice
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to spot, catch, and fix errors in short programs, and how to choose between fixing and catching.

lessons.title: Why Import
lessons.goal: This lesson covers why Python lets you import ready-made toolboxes called modules.

lessons.title: import module
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn the import statement, which loads a toolbox for your program to use.

lessons.title: module.name
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to call a tool with module.name after you import the module.

lessons.title: from import
lessons.goal: This lesson covers from module import name, so you can call a tool without typing the module name first.

lessons.title: random
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how to use random for chance events, with seed(1) so your practice rolls stay the same.

lessons.title: math Tools
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know some useful math module tools: sqrt, floor, ceil, and pi.

lessons.title: Combining Modules
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to use math and random together in one small program.

lessons.title: Mini Toolkit
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will build a tiny toolkit that mixes import styles and useful tools.

lessons.title: Why Classes
lessons.goal: This lesson covers why classes help you model real things that have their own data and actions.

lessons.title: Your First Class
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to write a tiny class using class and pass.

lessons.title: Objects
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how to make objects from a class by calling the class name with parentheses.

lessons.title: Attributes
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how attributes store data on each object, using a dot.

lessons.title: Methods
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how methods are functions inside a class that you call with a dot.

lessons.title: self
lessons.goal: By the end of this lesson you will know that self means this object inside a method.

lessons.title: __init__
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will learn how __init__ sets up an object's attributes as soon as you create it.

lessons.title: More __init__
lessons.goal: This lesson covers richer __init__ setups with more attributes, and starting values you set yourself.

lessons.title: Objects Together
lessons.goal: This lesson covers how several objects can work together in one program.

lessons.title: Designing with Classes
lessons.goal: In this lesson you will design a small program with a class that has data, __init__, and methods working together.
